nodes.name: NF cleaning
nodes.procedure: hydrochloric acid (2 M) was used to clean and remove impurities on the commercial nickel foam (NF, Kunshan Guangjiayuan New Materials Co. Ltd).
nodes.source_text: First, hydrochloric acid (2 M) was used to clean and remove impurities on the commercial nickel foam

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Mo-precursor deposition on NF
nodes.procedure: (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O (740 mg) was separately dispersed in 80 mL of deionized (DI) water. The mixture was transferred into an autoclave, and a piece of NF (4.5 cm × 4.5 cm) was vertically immersed into the solution and kept at 150 °C for 6 h. Then, Mo-based oxides were collected and dried.

nodes.name: Rapid carbothermal shocking to MoO2/NF
nodes.procedure: A rapid carbothermal shocking method (Joule-heat equipment: Hefei in situ technology Co., Ltd. China) and hydrogen reduction were applied to prepare MoO2/NF. A piece of Mo-based oxides (1 cm × 2 cm) was heated at 800 °C on a graphite heating plate for 133 seconds under Ar-H2 flow (Fig. S1, ESI†), and then, MoO2/NF (mass loading ∼5 mg cm^{-2}) was collected.

nodes.name: Anodic reconstruction to FeMoOOH
nodes.procedure: A typical three-electrode system was used to prepare FeMoOOH/NF. Among them, a carbon rod and a Hg/HgO electrode (SCE) were used as the counter electrode and the reference electrode, respectively. Then, MoO2/NF was placed in 1.0 M KOH solution with 0.28 mM Fe(NO3)3·9H2O as the working electrode. Subsequently, electrochemical anodic reconstruction was performed at a constant voltage (0.87 V vs. Hg/HgO) of 2 h to obtain the amorphous FeMoOOH/NF electrocatalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD curves show original MoO2 peaks disappeared and FeMoOOH/NF maintains amorphous structure after reconstruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) of FeMoOOH/NF with different reconstruction times (0 h, 0.5 h and 2 h) revealed that the crystal structure of FeMoOOH/NF was significantly altered and the original MoO2 peaks disappeared.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows dense nanosheet structure at 0 h, loose surface at 0.5 h, and deep reconstructed structure at 2 h for FeMoOOH/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At 0 h (before the stability test), the FeMoOOH/NF catalyst exhibited a dense structure (Fig. 2d). With the reconstruction process going on, the surface of the FeMoOOH/NF catalyst underwent rapid Mo dissolution and Fe substitution at 0.5 h, resulting in a loose surface structure (Fig. 2e).
